extracted.intended_audience: students and proctors of the 2025 AP Calculus AB exam (free-response sections)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and scoring-relevant rules for completing Section II (Parts A and B) of the 2025 AP Calculus AB free-response exam, including calculator policy, notation requirements, and expectations for showing work and justifying answers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show all work; answers scored on methods and correctness
rubrics_metrics.description: Show all of your work, even though a question may not explicitly remind you to do so. Your work will be scored on the correctness and completeness of your methods as well as your answers. Answers without supporting work will usually not receive credit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide intermediate steps and reasoning. Final numerical answers alone are generally insufficient; include the reasoning that leads to each answer so scorers can award method credit when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify uses of theorems/tests by verifying conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Justifications require that you give mathematical reasons and that you verify the needed conditions under which relevant theorems, properties, definitions, or tests are applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When invoking a theorem (e.g., Mean Value Theorem, FTC, tests for convergence), explicitly state and check the hypothesis (continuity, differentiability, integrability, etc.) before applying it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label subparts and any objects used
rubrics_metrics.description: For questions that have sub-parts, be sure to label those clearly in your solution. Clearly label any functions, graphs, tables, or other objects that you use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark part letters (A, B, C, ...) and label expressions, graphs, or tables referred to in your reasoning so graders can follow which part of the rubric your work addresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculator policy for Section II Part A
rubrics_metrics.description: Section II, Part A has 2 free-response questions and lasts 30 minutes. A graphing calculator is required for the questions on this part of the exam. You may use a handheld graphing calculator or the calculator available in this application. Make sure your calculator is in radian mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed to use calculator to solve equations, find derivatives at a point, or calculate definite integrals (see calculator-setup requirement below). Use radian mode for trigonometric computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: No calculator for Section II Part B
rubrics_metrics.description: Section II, Part B has 4 free-response questions and lasts 1 hour. A calculator is not allowed for this part of the exam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan your time and techniques accordingly — all work must be done without calculator assistance for Part B.

rubrics_metrics.name: When using a calculator, show the setup
rubrics_metrics.description: You are permitted to use your calculator to solve an equation, find the derivative of a function at a point, or calculate the value of a definite integral. However, you must clearly indicate the setup of your question, namely the equation, function, or integral you are using.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you used the calculator to obtain a numeric result, write the mathematical equation, derivative expression, or integral you computed so graders can see what was calculated.

rubrics_metrics.name: If using built-in features or programs, show mathematical steps
rubrics_metrics.description: If you use other built-in features or programs, you must show the mathematical steps necessary to produce your results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on a program's black-box output; explain the mathematical procedure the program is performing and include steps or justification that connect the program output to the answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use standard mathematical notation, not calculator syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: Your work must be expressed in standard mathematical notation rather than calculator syntax. For example, fnInt X X 15 may not be written as x dx.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write integrals, derivatives, limits, sums, etc., in conventional mathematical form. Avoid entering or copying calculator/menu commands as your solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and rounding expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise specified, answers (numeric or algebraic) need not be simplified. If you use decimal approximations in calculations, your work will be scored on accuracy. Unless otherwise specified, your final answers should be accurate to three places after the decimal point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When approximating, show how the approximation was obtained and give answers rounded (or accurate) to three decimal places unless the problem states a different requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain assumption for functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise specified, the domain of a function f is assumed to be the set of all real numbers x for which f(x) is a real number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the problem does not state a domain explicitly, assume the natural real domain (exclude values making expressions undefined) and state it when needed for justifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write answers in the free-response booklet and use permitted writing instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: You may use the available paper for scratch work, but you must write your answers in the free-response booklet. In the free-response booklet, write your solution to each part of each question in the space provided for that part. Use a pencil or a pen with black or dark blue ink.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not write final answers only on scratch paper. Put your labeled, complete solutions in the designated response spaces and use the permitted writing tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time/navigation rules during the section
rubrics_metrics.description: You can go back and forth between questions in this part until time expires. The clock will turn red when 5 minutes remain—the proctor will not give you any time updates or warnings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manage time across parts; be aware you will not receive verbal countdowns. Note the separate time limits for Part A (30 minutes) and Part B (1 hour).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicate units of measure where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: In problems that involve rates or quantities (e.g., words per minute), indicate units of measure for your numerical answers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include units (words, minutes, acres, etc.) on numeric answers when the problem context requires it so graders can award full credit for correct units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow problem-specific directions (setup, do not evaluate, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Problems sometimes request particular forms of responses (e.g., 'Show the setup for your calculations', 'Write, but do not evaluate, an integral expression'). Follow these instructions exactly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a prompt asks for an expression without evaluation, provide the correct integral/sum/limit/etc. and do not compute it; conversely, if asked to compute, show the evaluation steps.
